def: A loop in which production failures are captured, labelled and turned into permanent tests, so each turn leaves the system better protected.
The collection of test cases every candidate release must pass, built largely from failures already fixed.
A behaviour that used to be correct and is now wrong after a change.
An automatic check, usually in continuous integration, that blocks a change when the suite shows it got worse by a rule fixed in advance.
A named, recurring way a system goes wrong, counted across traces to decide what to fix first.
Labelled cases nobody has tuned against, used to check that improvements generalise beyond the regression suite.
A subset of test cases where a mistake is expensive, such as money, safety or privacy, tracked separately so averages cannot hide a failure.
A test case that passed on every repeated run before a change and fails on most runs after it.
Sending a small share of real traffic to a new version first and watching indicators before widening the rollout.
Running a candidate on a copy of live traffic and scoring its answers without showing them to users.
The finding that people's grading criteria change as they review outputs, because grading helps them define what they want.
The share of reviewed failures that belong to a failure mode already covered by a test case.
